documents.title: Setting Up Of A Leaf Spring Manufacturing Facility At The Existing Manufacturing Plant Under M/S. Jai Suspensions Limited, A Wholly Owned Subsidiary Of The Company.
Unaudited Financial Results For Half Year And Quarter Ended September 30, 2026

analysis.summary: For Q2 FY 2026-27, Jamna Auto Industries reported consolidated net sales of Rs 786 crore and an EBITDA of Rs 108 crore. The company completed its acquisition of Owen Springs Limited on September 1, 2026, and relocated its proposed 1,500 MT per month leaf spring line to Malanpur. Assembly operations at the Indore facility are ready and awaiting administrative approval expected in November 2026. Under its Lakshya RISE 5000 roadmap, Jamna Auto aims to reach Rs 5,000 crore in revenue with a 50% dividend payout by FY2029-30. Jamna Auto Industries reported that the Indian commercial vehicle industry demonstrated steady momentum during Q1, supporting its revenue performance in the M&HCV segment.

guidance.claim: Jamna Auto targets achieving Rs. 5,000 crores in revenue, 40% revenue from new markets, 40% ROCE, and a 50% dividend payout by FY 2029-30.
guidance.quote: Target is to achieve Rs. 5,000 crores Revenue, New Markets (Indian After Market + Export) to be 40% of Revenue, deliver 40% ROCE and 50% Dividend payout, by FY 2029-30.

guidance.claim: The proposed acquisition is part of the company's growth ambition to achieve 40% of turnover from new markets.
guidance.quote: A step toward 40% of turnover from new markets —part of JAI’s Lakshya RISE 5000 growth ambition.

Growth was supported by festive demand, improved affordability following the GST reformsandsustainedinfrastructureinvestment.

The Indian commercial vehicle industry demonstrated steady momentum in Q1 driven by positive underlying economic factors.
demand_outlook.quote: The Indian commercial vehicle industry demonstrated steady momentum during Q1, driven by positive underlying economic factors..

demand_outlook.quote: Looking ahead, the fundamental demand drivers for the commercial vehicle sector looks Positive supported by sustained infrastructure investments and favorable economic conditions

capex_expansion.quote: This proposed 1,500 MT per month conventional leaf spring line is being relocated from the subsidiary's Adityapur plant to the Company's existing Malanpur facility.
